 Abanikanda to serve as Cowboys’ RB2 vs. 49ers
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Israel Abanikanda 
 DAL 
 Running Back 
 #25 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Israel Abanikanda will serve as the team’s RB2 in Week 10 against the 49ers.
 Abanikanda will get the practice squad elevation over Kendre Miller, who recently signed with the team after being released by the Saints. Abanikanda has spent part of the last two seasons with the Cowboys and had a solid preseason, rushing for 91 scoreless yards on 22 carries while adding three receptions for 16 yards. We wouldn’t expect Abanikanda to see enough meaningful work to be fantasy relevant this week but he could be worth a stash in deeper leagues as insurance for Javonte Williams.
 -  Zachary Krueger 
 Source:  Todd Archer

 Cowboys declared WR Camden Brown, RB Israel Abanikanda, OLB Tyrus Wheat, CB Caelen Carson, and OT Ajani Cornelius inactive for Week 1 against the Giants. 
 Javonte Williams should see all the volume he can handle with the Cowboys entering Week 1 with a recent signee and a practice squad elevation as depth behind their lead back. There weren’t any other surprises outside of the lack of backfield depth. 
 Malik Davis 
 DAL 
 Running Back 
 #20 
 ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that Cowboys Malik Davis (hip) will have surgery and be placed on injured reserve. 
 It is unclear whether this is a season-ending injury or if Davis has a chance to return later in the year. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier that the Cowboys were “bracing for an extended absence” and that a source told him, “it’s bad.” It sounds like Davis’ 2026 season may be over. Cowboys RB Emari Demercado now sits behind starting RB Javonte Williams, and RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad. 
 Malik Davis 
 DAL 
 Running Back 
 #20 
 ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday. 
 Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

 The Cowboys also released/waived LB Justin Barron, RB Jaydon Blue, CB Trikweze Bridges, CB Josh Butler, S Zion Childress, RB Jashaun Corbin, DT Tommy Dunn, G Chris Glaser, T Sebastian Gutierrez, WR Jordan Hudson, T Marcellus Johnson, G Trevor Keegan, TE Zack Kuntz, LB Isaiah Land, RB Phil Mafah, DT Dayo Odeleye, LB Langston Patterson, T Shiyazh Pete, WR Anthony Smith, WR Jaden Smith, CB Reddy Steward, DT Jay Toia, TE Michael Trigg, TE Mitch Van Vooren, G DJ Wingfield, DT DJ Withers, S Julius Wood, WR Tyler Johnson, CB Derioin Kendrick, WR Denzel Mims, LB Curtis Robinson, WR Marquez Valeds-Scantling, LB Sam Williams, TE DJ Rogers and placed LB Marist Liufau and CB Devin Moore. 
 Malik Davis 
 DAL 
 Running Back 
 #20 
 Cowboys RB Malik Davis was held out with the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Saints. 
 Davis appears to have secured a roster spot, but we won’t know for sure until Sunday. The broadcast initially referred to him as the starter, but it was instead RB Phil Mafah who took the field. Mafah dominated backfield touches throughout the first half, repeatedly running into Saints defenders on runs up the middle. He was spelled by RB Israel Abanikanda. Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue does not seem to be playing this evening. Last Sunday, The Athletic’s Jon Machota predicted Blue would seize the No. 2 running back job from Davis in-season. 
 Jaydon Blue 
 DAL 
 Running Back 
 #23 
 Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue (shoulder) resumed participating in team drills on Thursday. 
 The good news is that Blue took “some” snaps in team drills for the first time this week, according to ESPN’s Todd Archer. The bad news is that Blue was the fourth player up behind starting RB Javonte Williams and fellow backups RB Malik Davis and RB Israel Abanikanda. Earlier today, COO and co-owner Stephen Jones said Blue and RB Phil Mafah were being “pushed” by Davis. While it’s possible the team is just easing Blue back into action, his spot in the rotation, coupled with Jones’ comments, is concerning. He had received positive reviews to this point, but a fantasy-related reassessment may be in order. The backfield rotation in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cardinals is worth tracking.

 Packers signed WR Mecole Hardman to their practice squad. 
 Hardman was waived at last cuts but decided that staying with the Packers made sense. The 27-year-old will likely be elevated in Week 1 if Jayden Reed’s injury is as serious as it seems. Also joining the Packers practice squad are: QB Clayton Tune, RB Israel Abanikanda, DL Deslin Alexandre, DB Johnathan Baldwin, T Brant Banks, DL James Ester, LB Jamon Johnson, K Mark McNamee, DL Arron Mosby, WR Isaiah Neyor, WR Will Sheppard, DB Jaylin Simpson, and LB Kristian Welch.

The Packers placed C/G Jacob Monk placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. 
 Israel Abanikanda 
 GB 
 Running Back 
 #20 
 Packers signed RB Israel Abanikanda, formerly of the 49ers, to a contract. 
 Abanikanda moves from one Shanahan system to another. Unfortunately, for the one-cut-and-go runner, the Packers’ running back unit is even deeper than the 49ers’. He is unlikely to find a fantasy-relevant role in Green Bay. 
 Quintez Cephus 
 SF 
 Wide Receiver 
 #2 
 49ers signed WR Quintez Cephus. 
 Cephus has not played an NFL game since 2022, when he caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards. He is not guaranteed to make the final roster and does not need to be considered as a late-round option. The team waived RB Israel Abanikanda in a corresponding move.

 Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
 Week 10 will be one for Meyers to forget. He dropped a deep shot from Trevor Lawrence on a trick play. Lawrence, admittedly, underthrew the ball, forcing Meyers to turn around and fight through contact at the catch point. Meyers dropped another touchdown later in the game that was more than catchable. Meyers hasn’t scored since Week 3 and has caught more than five passes in two games this year. He’s struggling to provide even WR4 value ahead of the Jags’ Week 11 matchup with the Giants. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints. 
 Waller ran a route on 27 of the team’s 38 drop backs and should have caught what would have been a 30-yard touchdown in the first half. Coming off a big game in Week 9 against the Broncos, Waller was fourth on the team in targets as the Panthers turned hard toward the run. Tommy Tremble had more targets, receptions, and yards than Waller on the day. Waller’s red zone role and the Panthers usual pass heaviness should keep him viable as a streaming option in Week 11 against Baltimore. 
 -  Denny Carter

 Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-2 targets for 3 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
 Sadiq is becoming buried on the Jets’ depth chart. He did run a route on 23 dropbacks in this one, compared to 28 for Mason Taylor, but Taylor played 23 more snaps, and Sadiq also has to compete with three receivers for targets. He can’t be trusted in fantasy leagues right now and should not be on redraft rosters unless there’s an injury.

 Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
 BTJ split the WR3 duties with Josh Cameron once again. Cameron, however, racked up 67 yards and a touchdown on three grabs. Thomas hasn’t even topped 40 yards in a game this year. He’s a part-time decoy who spends most of his routes clearing out space for Parker Washington. With the trade deadline in the rearview mirror, fantasy managers can safely send BTJ to the waiver wire on the upcoming run.

 Dalton Schultz caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
 Schultz’s only grab of the game was Houston’s only score of the second half, a ball C.J. Stroud lofted over zone coverage in the end zone to find Schultz at the back of it. It was a low-end outcome for Schultz, who had his lowest target count of the season. He’ll remain a high-end TE2 play against the Colts in Week 11 on Thursday.

 Seth McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
 McGowan eclipsed his previous career-high with 12 carries in the Colts’ win. He continues to be involved, eating into Jonathan Taylor’s workload with a few red zone carries and a four-yard rushing touchdown to open the second quarter. McGowan was not involved in the passing game and Taylor still saw 23 more snaps. However, it seems like McGowan is here to stay as a playmaker for the Colts offense with a rushing score for the second straight game. He should be on fantasy rosters as a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 11 against the Texans.
 -  Aditya Fuldeore

It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

 He added a zero-yard carry. His longest catch was for 29 yards. That about sums up his other four targets. Dell wasn’t able to shake man coverage very often and the Browns put the clamps on in the second half. He managed just 33-of-67 snaps. He’ll remain on the FLEX line against the Colts on Thursday night in what should be a more zone-heavy game.

 Chris Rodriguez rushed four times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
 Rodriguez spent most of the day watching Bhayshul Tuten rack up a career-high 29 touches, 26 of which were carries. Tuten also saw all the goal line work and eventually found the end zone late in the fourth quarter. With Tuten’s role on the rise, fantasy managers can likely cut ties with Rodriguez ahead of Week 11. He will be buried in the RB4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants.

 Isaiah Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
 Williams stepped into a bigger role with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) leaving this game after the Jets’ first offensive play. The 25-year-old could have had a bigger day, but a long catch-and-run was called back due to offsetting penalties. If Cooper Jr. were to miss Week 11, Williams could be a deep league FLEX option against the Chargers, but he’s likely not in for a huge role.
